title: Internal structure of string
concept: string stores data on the heap, and size and capacity are tracked separately.

steps.title: Create a short string
steps.explanation: `"Hi"` is a two-letter character, and in many implementations, Small String Optimization (SSO) is applied and stored inside the object without heap allocation.

steps.title: size and capacity
steps.explanation:
`size` is the current number of characters (2), `capacity` is the maximum size it can hold without reallocation.

Capacity is fixed within the SSO range (usually 15 to 22 bytes).

steps.title: string expansion
steps.explanation: `s += " World!"` makes the string longer. When the SSO scope is exceeded, it allocates a new buffer on the heap and copies the data.

quiz.question: What is Small String Optimization (SSO)?
options: Optimization to always store strings on the heap
Optimization to avoid heap allocation by storing short strings inside objects
Optimization to make string comparisons faster
Optimization for compressed storage of strings
quiz.explanation: SSO avoids unnecessary heap allocation by storing short strings (usually 15 to 22 bytes) in memory in the string object itself.

misconceptions.correct: Thanks to SSO, short strings are stored on the stack (inside the object).
misconceptions.why: Heap allocations are expensive, so we apply optimizations to short strings.

keyTakeaway: String distinguishes between size (current length) and capacity (allocation size), and optimizes the performance of short strings with SSO.
